newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, led by silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, led by silver.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Thursday, led by a sharp fall in silver prices to 18 month month lows.

"There was no change in the fundamentals, just some fund selling and stop executions which fed on themselves when silver failed to quickly bounce back from the break of $5.00," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.

COMEX December silver ended down 15.8 cents at $4.940 an ounce, after seeing an 18 month low for the December contract intraday at $4.925. In the bullion market, spot silver saw an 18 month low also at $4.90 an ounce.
But December silver now looks oversold and may see a bounce from current levels, with the standard nine-day relative strength indicator (RSI) closing at 22 percent Thursday.
"Prospects for another large shortfall between world supply and demand should prevent silver prices from dropping much below the $5.00 level," Rinehimer said.
"The level of Japanese silver imports is also recovering," he noted.
COMEX December gold ended 70 cents lower at $385.60, just up from an intraday low at $385.40.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $382.50/383.00, from a London afternoon fix Thursday at $382.75, and a New York close Wednesday at $383.15.
"Renewed technical selling is expected to push gold back to $382 later in the week, with speculators and dealers looking to test the $380 support," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"Should U.S. equity markets remain strong, gold prices will remain susceptible to such selling."
NYMEX October platinum ended down $2.00 cents at $390.50, after recovering earlier this week from a two month low at $388.60 seen Monday.
NYMEX December palladium ended down 75 cents at $121.75, after seeing a fresh life-of-contract low at $120.75 early in the session.
"Fabrication demand for both metals (platinum and palladium) is strong, but few fabricators are likely to buy into a weak or falling market," Kempf said.
